slides.text: Most AI tools feel like a mediocre contractor who doesn't get your work.
slides.voiceover_text: Ever feel like most AI tools are just a mediocre contractor who doesn't really get what you do? There's a reason.

slides.text: Check it fits your process, not a generic FAQ script.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip one: check it fits your actual process, not some generic frequently asked questions script.

slides.text: Ask if it handles exceptions like a trained team member.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip two: ask whether it handles the awkward exceptions the way a trained team member would.

slides.text: Pick tools that reduce your task list, not add to it.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip three: pick tools that shrink your task list, not ones that add another job to manage.

slides.text: Real help is a process partner, not another output generator to manage.
slides.voiceover_text: So remember: real help is a process partner, not another output generator you have to babysit.

youtubeTitle: Why Most AI Tools Feel Like Cheap Outsourcing
youtubeDescription: Most AI tools feel like a mediocre contractor who doesn't get your work. Output generators add to your task list. Process partners understand your workflow and actually reduce it.
geo_answer: Most AI tools disappoint because they are output generators that produce results from prompts, whereas genuinely useful tools are process partners that understand and integrate into your actual workflow.
geo_takeaways: An output generator gives you something to check, fix and manage, so it adds to your workload rather than reducing it.
A process partner understands the steps, decision points and exceptions of your workflow, like a trained team member.
Generic chatbots built for e-commerce give service-business callers a poor experience, so prospects hang up and call a competitor.
